steps: Confirm the selected Namespace and inspect its complete RoleBinding inventory with the RBAC owner.
If a local binding is required, review the intended subjects and Role permissions before adding a scoped RoleBinding through the owned manifest.
Verify the binding subjects and access in the intended environment; remove or revise the new binding if it grants unintended access.
k8s_namespace_has_rolebinding.summary: Review the selected Namespace RBAC intent and add a scoped RoleBinding only if approved.

steps: Confirm the two required label keys and values with the namespace and policy owners; inspect the collected Namespace metadata.
Update the owned Namespace manifest with the approved labels and review selectors that may use them.
Verify the Namespace labels and selector behavior after rollout; restore the previous manifest if workload selection changes unexpectedly.
k8s_namespace_namespace_part_specific_la.summary: Set the two approved Namespace labels in the owned manifest after selector review.

steps: Confirm the approved namespace set and the affected LoadBalancer Service identity and ownership.
Review traffic, DNS, provider annotations, and namespace dependencies before moving/recreating the Service or changing the approved policy.
Verify availability and approved placement after rollout; restore the prior owner-approved Service configuration if traffic breaks.
k8s_service_loadbalancers_associated_aut.summary: Review LoadBalancer Service placement against the approved Namespace set.

steps: Confirm the owner-required Service type and inspect the observed Service type and endpoint usage.
Review exposure and availability impact, then update spec.type in the owned manifest only if the policy is correct for this Service.
Verify endpoint behavior after rollout and roll back the manifest revision if traffic is disrupted.
k8s_service_services_type_specified_rule.summary: Align the Service type with the owner policy after traffic-impact review.

field_binding.path: complete Service metadata.namespace/name/uid and spec.type compared with operator-selected identities

steps: Confirm the selected Service namespace, name and UID still match the owner approval; a recreated UID needs renewed approval.
Review external exposure, provider annotations, and dependent traffic with the Service owner before changing spec.type to LoadBalancer.
Verify Service and load balancer provisioning and traffic after rollout; restore the previous manifest if the change is unsuitable.
k8s_service_spec_type_loadbalancer.summary: Use LoadBalancer type only for the currently approved exact Service identity.
